label: [R] numbers read from the papers, never results of ours. They are printed next to the official re-runs for orientation only and must not be copied into FICL result tables.
how_read: Read on 2026-11-24 from the arXiv versions listed below through an automated text extraction of the PDF / HTML. Confirm each value against the PDF before quoting it (open item P1 in docs/OFFICIAL_REPRO.md).

fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r.paper: Fani et al., Accelerating Heterogeneous FL with Closed-form Classifiers, ICML 2024, arXiv:2406.01116v1
fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r.caption: Final accuracy (%) of the FED3R family of classifiers and FedNCM on the Cifar100 dataset.
fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r.setting: CIFAR-100, 100 clients each holding one class (alpha = 0, Hsu et al. 2019), MobileNetV2 pre-trained on ImageNet, images scaled to 224x224, lambda = 0.01

fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r_rf5k.caption: Final accuracy (%) of the FED3R family of classifiers and FedNCM on the Cifar100 dataset.
fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r_rf5k.setting: as fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r; random features D = 5000, sigma = 1000

fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r_rf10k.caption: Final accuracy (%) of the FED3R family of classifiers and FedNCM on the Cifar100 dataset.
fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r_rf10k.setting: as fed3r_icml24_t6_fed3r; random features D = 10000, sigma = 1000

fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fedncm.paper: Goswami et al., Covariances for Free, NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2412.14326v3
fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fedncm.caption: Evaluation of different training-free methods using 100 clients for first four datasets
fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fedncm.setting: CIFAR-100, 100 clients, Dirichlet alpha = 0.1, ViT-B/16 (d = 768), 5 random seeds

fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fed3r.caption: Evaluation of different training-free methods using 100 clients for first four datasets
fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fed3r.setting: as fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fedncm; Fed3R as implemented in the FedCOF repository (no bias column)

fedcof_neurips25_t3_vit_fedcof.caption: Evaluation of different training-free methods using 100 clients for first four datasets

afl_cvpr25_t2_cifar100.paper: He et al., AFL, CVPR 2025, arXiv:2405.16240v2
afl_cvpr25_t2_cifar100.caption: The top-1 accuracy (%) of compared methods under two non-IID settings.
afl_cvpr25_t2_cifar100.setting: CIFAR-100, 100 clients, ResNet-18 pre-trained on ImageNet-1k, gamma = 1 with RI, 3 runs; identical for alpha = 0.1, 0.01 and s = 10, 5

stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsa_final.paper: Guan et al., STSA, WWW 2026, arXiv:2506.01327v3
stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsa_final.caption: Experimental results for training from pre-trained model (ViT-B/16) with varying levels of data heterogeneity.
stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsa_final.setting: CIFAR-100, T = 10 tasks, K = 5 clients, beta = 0.5, ViT-B/16 IN-21K with adapter, first stage 10 rounds x 2 local epochs, M = 1250, ridge 1e6

stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsa_avg.caption: Experimental results for training from pre-trained model (ViT-B/16) with varying levels of data heterogeneity.

stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsae_final.caption: Experimental results for training from pre-trained model (ViT-B/16) with varying levels of data heterogeneity.
stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsae_final.setting: as stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsa_final; the paper states K_D = 10, the released main.py sets dummy = 5

stsa_www26_t2_b05_stsae_avg.caption: Experimental results for training from pre-trained model (ViT-B/16) with varying levels of data heterogeneity.
